```text
# 23 Resize main view when side panel is open open 
 **Summary**

When the side navigation panel is opened via the hamburger menu, it overlays the main budget view rather than pushing or resizing it. Content beneath the panel remains rendered at full width but is partially obscured by the panel. The main content area should reflow to occupy only the remaining visible space while the panel is open, ensuring no information is hidden behind it at any screen size where both can reasonably coexist.

**User Story**

As a user who opens the side panel while reviewing my budget, I want the main content area to resize so that it fits alongside the open panel so that I can still see and interact with my budget data without the panel covering it up.

**User Scenario**

Someone would encounter/use this feature by opening the side panel; the main content area should then resize so that the side panel doesn't cover any information.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. When the side panel is open, the main content to the right should reflow to use the remaining space on-screen so that no information is obscured.
2. When the side panel is closed, the main content should return to its existing layout and available width.
3. The main content should remain fully visible and interactive while the side panel is open.
4. Opening or closing the side panel should not cause the main content to become horizontally clipped or inaccessible.

## Out of Scope
- Redesigning the side navigation or budget view.
- Changing existing navigation or budget functionality.
- Changing the contents or styling of either the side panel or main budget view unless required for the layout fix.
- **Defining new behavior for viewport sizes where the side panel and main content cannot reasonably coexist; this will be addressed separately.**
- Fixing unrelated responsive, overflow, or layout issues elsewhere in the application.

## Open Questions
- What should happen when the side panel is open if with a smaller viewport width there isn't enough space for all content to be visible?



**Rough Scope**

Large — The core change is a layout adjustment: the main content area needs to respond to the panel's open state, either by reducing its width or shifting its offset to accommodate the panel's footprint. If the layout is already flex or grid-based this may be relatively contained, but if the panel is currently positioned absolutely or fixed outside the normal document flow, the main content area will need structural changes to participate in the same layout context. Care is also needed at smaller viewport widths where there may not be enough room for both panel and content to coexist. A beginner contributor should audit the current panel positioning strategy and the main layout's structure before writing any code, as the right fix depends heavily on how these two elements are currently composed.

**Source**

Directly observed behavior. Consistent with standard side-drawer layout patterns where content reflow is the expected behavior. Assisted with Claude for issue generation. 
---
# 68 Audit layout structure and refactor side panel into the layout flow closed 
 ## Summary
Audit how the side panel and main budget view are currently positioned, then restructure them so both participate in the same layout context (e.g., a flex or grid container) instead of the panel overlaying the content. This issue delivers the structural foundation only, with no visible resizing behavior required yet.

## User Story
As a developer, I want the side panel and main content to share a common layout container so that the main content can respond to the panel's open state.

## Tasks

- Document how the panel is currently positioned (absolute, fixed, or in-flow) and how the main layout is composed
- Wrap the panel and main content in a shared flex/grid container
~~- Remove or replace absolute/fixed positioning that takes the panel out of flow~~ Moved to issue #69 as it would go against the acceptance criteria that the panel remain exactly as before
- Expose the panel's open/closed state so the layout can consume it

## Acceptance Criteria
- The panel and main content live in the same layout context.
- The panel opens and closes exactly as before, with no change to its contents or styling.
- No regressions to existing navigation or budget functionality.
- Findings from the audit are written up in the issue or PR for reviewers.  
---
# 70 Verify layout across viewport sizes and document narrow-screen behavior open 
 ## Summary
Test the resize behavior across the range of viewport widths where the panel and content can reasonably coexist, fix any edge-case overflow or clipping found, and surface the open question about very narrow viewports so it can be handled separately.

## User Story
As a user on different screen sizes, I want the panel and budget view to coexist cleanly wherever there is room, so that I can trust that no content is hidden.

## Tasks

- Manually test at common desktop, laptop, and tablet widths, with the panel both open and closed
- Fix layout issues in the budget view that are caused by the reduced width (only where required for this fix)
- Add automated coverage where practical (e.g., component or visual regression tests for open/closed states)
- Identify the viewport width at which the panel and content stop coexisting reasonably, and file a separate follow-up issue for that behavior
- Record test results and screenshots in the PR

## Acceptance Criteria

- At every supported width where both can coexist, no content is obscured or clipped in either state.
- Open/closed states are covered by at least basic automated or documented manual tests.
- A follow-up issue exists for narrow-viewport behavior, answering the open question, and is linked from this one.
- No unrelated responsive or overflow issues are modified.
```

```text
import React from 'react';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';
import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';

import { Sidebar } from './Sidebar';
import { useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

export function FloatableSidebar() {
  const sidebar = useSidebar();
  const { isNarrowWidth } = useResponsive();

  const sidebarShouldFloat = sidebar.floating;

  return isNarrowWidth ? null : (
    <View
      onMouseOver={
        sidebarShouldFloat
          ? e => {
              e.stopPropagation();
              sidebar.setHoveringSidebar(true);
            }
          : undefined
      }
      onMouseLeave={
        sidebarShouldFloat ? () => sidebar.setHoveringSidebar(false) : undefined
      }
      style={{
        position: sidebarShouldFloat ? 'absolute' : undefined,
        top: 8,
        // If not floating, the -50 takes into account the transform below
        bottom: sidebarShouldFloat ? 8 : -50,
        zIndex: 1001,
        borderRadius: sidebarShouldFloat ? '0 6px 6px 0' : 0,
        overflow: 'hidden',
        boxShadow:
          !sidebarShouldFloat || sidebar.hidden
            ? 'none'
            : '0 15px 30px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.25), 0 3px 15px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.5)',
        transform: `translateY(${!sidebarShouldFloat ? -8 : 0}px)
                      translateX(${
                        sidebarShouldFloat && sidebar.hidden ? '-100' : '0'
                      }%)`,
        transition:
          'transform .5s, box-shadow .5s, border-radius .5s, bottom .5s',
      }}
    >
      <Sidebar />
    </View>
  );
}
import React from 'react';
import type { ComponentPropsWithoutRef, CSSProperties } from 'react';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
```

I'd call #69 **small to medium**. The code change is small, maybe 50–100 lines across 3–4 files plus tests. The part that needs care is how hover-to-open interacts with content that reflows, not the layout itself.

## Where things stand after #68

The layout is already in shape for this. In [FinancesApp.tsx:203-219](packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancesApp.tsx#L203-L219), `<FloatableSidebar />` and the main content are siblings in a `flexDirection: 'row'` container, and the main content has `flex: 1`.

- **Pinned mode** (`floatingSidebar` off) already does what #69 asks. The sidebar is in normal layout flow, so the content reflows around it.
- **Floating mode** is the only one that overlays. [sidebar/index.tsx:28-45](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx#L28-L45) sets `position: 'absolute'` and hides the sidebar by sliding it off-screen with `translateX(-100%)`. The content never gives up any width, so the open sidebar covers it.

So #69 comes down to this: when floating mode is open, take up layout space the way pinned mode does.

## Likely changes

1. **[sidebar/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx)** (the core change): drop `position: absolute` in floating mode and animate how much space the sidebar takes up instead, e.g. `marginLeft: hidden ? -width : 0` or `width: hidden ? 0 : width` with `flexShrink: 0`. Animating a real width is also what keeps the transition from causing horizontal clipping or scrolling.
2. **[SidebarProvider.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx)** and **[Sidebar.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx)**: the sidebar's width is currently local state inside `Sidebar.tsx` (resizable, 200px up to a third of the window, default 240). The wrapper needs that number to animate, so move it into the provider and expose it next to `hidden` and `floating`. This is a small refactor.
3. **[Titlebar.tsx:295-297](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx#L295-L297)**: the Electron/macOS `paddingLeft: 80` leaves room for the window buttons on the assumption that the titlebar starts at the window's left edge. Once the content shifts right, that assumption breaks, so it probably needs an `&& sidebar.hidden` condition. The box-shadow and border-radius in floating mode are overlay styling and may need adjusting too.
4. **Tests**: update `index.test.tsx` (it already covers floating vs pinned) and `SidebarProvider.test.ts`.

## Main risk: hover-to-open

Floating mode opens on hover over the hamburger button and closes 350ms after the mouse leaves. If opening also pushes the content:

- The hamburger button lives in the titlebar, inside the content area, so it slides away from the cursor as the content reflows.
- Just passing the mouse over the hamburger would push the whole budget sideways and back. That's jarring, and it could flicker as hover state toggles.

The team should settle this before coding. Possible options:
- **(a)** Reflow on every open, including hover. This is the most literal reading of the acceptance criteria and the most jarring.
- **(b)** Hover still overlays as it does now; clicking or tapping opens it "sticky" and reflows.
- **(c)** Recognise that pinned mode already does this and frame #69 as "opening the panel pins it".

I'd go with (b), but it's really a decision for whoever wrote the issue.

## Out of scope

- Below 668px (`alwaysFloats`), I'd keep the overlay. #23 explicitly defers narrow-viewport behaviour, and #70 owns testing across widths and any budget-table overflow at reduced width.
- No pages need structural changes. `settings/index.tsx` and `banksync/index.tsx` key centering off `floatingSidebar`, but `marginInline: auto` still works in a narrower container.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-05 23:11:42Z)**_

"Reflow" means the browser recalculates the layout because the space available to the main content has changed. The content then gets re-laid out to fit the new width. Here's what that means in Actual today.

## What happens now

The window is split into two flex children ([FinancesApp.tsx:203-219](packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancesApp.tsx#L203-L219)):

```
┌──────────────────── window (1200px) ────────────────────┐
│ [sidebar] [ main content: flex: 1                     ] │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Pinned mode:** the sidebar is a normal flex child, about 240px wide. The main content gets whatever is left (1200 − 240 = 960px), and the budget table lays itself out in 960px. Toggling pinned mode reflows the content to the new width. This already works.

**Floating mode:** the sidebar has `position: absolute`, which takes it out of the flex layout. The main content gets the full 1200px. Opening the sidebar slides it in on top of the content, and the content doesn't move:

```
closed:  [ main content 1200px ............................ ]
open:    [sidebar]ent 1200px ...............................]
          ^^^^^^^ covers the first 240px of the budget
```

That is the bug in #69: nothing reflows, so the left part of the budget sits hidden under the panel.

## What reflow would look like

If the open floating sidebar took up layout space, the content would shrink from 1200px to 960px and shift right:

```
closed:  [ main content 1200px ............................ ]
open:    [sidebar][ main content 960px .................... ]
```

Everything in the content area re-lays out at the new width. Budget columns narrow, text may wrap or truncate, and the titlebar (with the hamburger button) moves right by 240px. Animating the sidebar's width over 0.5s makes this a smooth squeeze rather than a jump, but the content still moves.

## Why hover matters

In floating mode, the sidebar opens when you **hover** over the hamburger button and closes 350ms after the mouse leaves. With reflow:

1. You move the mouse to the hamburger in the top-left corner.
2. The sidebar starts opening and the content, including the titlebar and the hamburger, slides 240px right.
3. The hamburger has moved out from under your cursor, and the sidebar is now under it. That's probably fine for hover tracking, because the sidebar has its own hover handler.
4. Moving the mouse back toward the budget closes the sidebar, and everything slides 240px back left.

So just brushing past the top-left corner squeezes the whole budget and then expands it again. Things you're looking at, or about to click, move under your cursor. This is why hover menus usually overlay content instead of pushing it.

## The three options

**(a) Reflow on every open, including hover.** Do exactly what's described above. It meets the acceptance criteria literally, but the budget jumps sideways whenever the mouse passes the corner.

**(b) Hover overlays; click opens "sticky" and reflows.**
- Hover over the hamburger: the sidebar peeks out on top of the content as it does now, with no reflow. This is a quick glance that goes away on its own.
- Click or tap the hamburger: the sidebar opens and stays open, and the content shrinks to fit beside it. Clicking again closes it, and the content expands back.

This needs a new piece of state in `SidebarProvider` to tell "peeking" apart from "opened". The content only gives up space when the sidebar is opened deliberately.

**(c) Opening it pins it.** Pinned mode already reflows correctly, so instead of building a new "open but not pinned" state, clicking the hamburger switches the sidebar to pinned mode, and the existing unpin button sends it back to floating. This needs the least new code. The downside is that pinning is saved as a global preference (`floatingSidebar`), so "opening" the sidebar would be remembered across sessions. That's probably not what the issue author meant by opening the panel.

## Why I lean toward (b)

It meets the user story ("nothing is hidden behind the panel" when the user opens it to work alongside the budget). It doesn't turn incidental mouse movement into layout jumps, and it doesn't overload the pin preference. But (a) is the most literal reading of the acceptance criteria. If your team or the issue author expects (a), it's worth checking with them before you build (b).

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-05 23:13:52Z)**_

**(a):** Whenever the sidebar opens, including when you just hover over the menu button, the budget shrinks to make room. When it closes, the budget grows back. Moving your mouse past the top-left corner makes the budget slide over and back.

**(b):** There are two ways to open the sidebar:
- **Hover** over the menu button: the sidebar slides out on top of the budget, as it does now. The budget doesn't move, and the sidebar disappears when your mouse leaves.
- **Click** the menu button: the sidebar opens and stays open, and the budget shrinks so nothing is covered. Click again to close it, and the budget grows back.

The difference is that in (a) any opening pushes the budget aside, while in (b) only a deliberate click does.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-05 23:16:00Z)**_

This is because of how floating mode works today, combined with what (a) adds.

**Today:**
- The menu button sits in the top-left corner of the budget page.
- Hovering over it opens the sidebar. You don't have to click ([Titlebar.tsx:305-310](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx#L305-L310)).
- The sidebar slides out under your cursor and closes about 350ms after your mouse leaves it ([SidebarProvider.tsx:60-67](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx#L60-L67)).

So if your mouse passes over the menu button on its way somewhere else, say to the account list or a budget cell near the top-left, the sidebar briefly pops open and then closes. Right now that doesn't matter much, because the sidebar just appears on top of the budget and disappears again. The budget never moves.

**With (a),** every open shrinks the budget and every close grows it back. That accidental pass over the button now looks like this:

1. The mouse crosses the menu button, and the sidebar opens.
2. The budget squeezes about 240px to the right to make room.
3. The mouse keeps moving and leaves the sidebar.
4. About 350ms later, the sidebar closes and the budget slides back to the left.

You didn't mean to open anything, but the whole budget shifted right and back. If you were aiming for something on the page, it moved while you were reaching for it.

That's why (b) only reflows on a click. A click is deliberate, and hovering can happen by accident.

_**User (2026-10-05 23:17:41Z)**_

couldn't this issue be fixed by blocking the menu button hover from doing anything until any playing animation is complete?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-05 23:17:51Z)**_

Partly. A lock like that fixes one problem but not the main one.

**What the lock would fix: loops while things are moving.** During the slide, the menu button moves too, so it can end up under the cursor again by accident. For example:

1. The sidebar is closing and the budget slides back left.
2. The menu button slides back under the resting cursor.
3. That counts as a new hover, so the sidebar reopens, the budget slides right again, and so on.

Ignoring hovers until the animation finishes would stop this bouncing. It's worth adding if you go with (a).

**What it wouldn't fix: the first accidental hover.** When nothing is animating, the lock isn't active, so the first time the mouse brushes the button the full sequence still happens:

- the sidebar opens and the budget slides right
- the mouse leaves and the budget slides back

The lock only blocks *repeat* triggers. It doesn't change the fact that one passing hover moves the whole page.

**What would fix that: a hover delay**, sometimes called "hover intent". The sidebar only opens if the cursor *rests* on the button for about 200–300ms. A mouse passing on its way somewhere else doesn't trigger it, but someone who stops on the button does. It's a small change: start a timer on hover, cancel it if the mouse leaves first.

**Where that leaves (a):** a hover delay plus your animation lock would make it much more usable. The one remaining issue is deliberate peeking. Someone who hovers just to glance at the sidebar still squeezes the budget over and back each time. Whether that's acceptable is a judgement call, and (b) avoids it entirely. If your team prefers (a), the delay and the lock together make it a reasonable choice.

```text
import { useCallback, useRef } from 'react';

export function useResizeObserver<T extends Element>(
  func: (contentRect: DOMRectReadOnly) => void,
): (el: T) => void {
  const observer = useRef<ResizeObserver | undefined>(undefined);
  if (!observer.current) {
    observer.current = new ResizeObserver(entries => {
      func(entries[0].contentRect);
    });
  }

  const elementRef = useCallback((el: T) => {
    observer.current?.disconnect();
    if (el) {
      observer.current?.observe(el, { box: 'border-box' });
    }
  }, []);

  return elementRef;
}
```

**Between 512px and 668px wide, the sidebar is forced into floating mode (`alwaysFloats`). Should opening it reflow the content at those widths too?**

Options:
- **Keep overlay (Recommended)** - Only reflow when the window is at least 668px. Parent issue #23 leaves narrow-screen behaviour out of scope, and #70 owns it. At 600px, a 200px+ sidebar would leave about 400px for the budget.
- **Reflow at all widths** - Reflow whenever floating mode opens, including between 512 and 668px. The narrow-screen squeeze would then be dealt with in #70.

**Which hover actions should be ignored while the sidebar is animating open or closed?**

Options:
- **Menu button only (Recommended)** - Only hovering the hamburger button is ignored. That's the button that slides under the cursor and can cause open/close loops. Moving back onto the sidebar while it's closing still reopens it, as it does today.
- **Menu button + sidebar** - Hovering the sidebar itself is also ignored during the animation, so a sidebar that has started closing always finishes closing.

**Should tapping or clicking the menu button (the touch toggle) also be ignored during the animation?**

Options:
- **No, taps always work (Recommended)** - A tap is deliberate, so it can reverse an animation that's in progress. Only hover is blocked, as you described.
- **Yes, block taps too** - Taps are ignored until the 0.5s animation finishes, the same as hover.


**Answer:** Keep overlay (Recommended), Menu button only (Recommended), No, taps always work (Recommended)

```markdown
# Plan: Issue #69 — Reflow main content when the floating sidebar opens (approach a)

## Context

In floating mode, `FloatableSidebar` is `position: absolute` and slides in with `translateX`, so it covers the left ~240px of the budget instead of taking up layout space. Pinned mode already reflows correctly because the sidebar and the main content are siblings in a flex row ([FinancesApp.tsx:203-219](packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancesApp.tsx#L203-L219); #68 established this).

Issue #69 asks for the main content to shrink whenever the panel opens and to grow back when it closes. We're implementing approach **(a)**: reflow on every open, hover included. Two safeguards make that usable:
- **200ms hover delay** on the menu (hamburger) button, so a mouse passing over it doesn't open the sidebar.
- **Animation lock**: hovering the menu button does nothing while the 0.5s open/close animation is running. This stops loops caused by the button sliding back under a still cursor.

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Narrow widths:** reflow only for the `floatingSidebar` preference when `!alwaysFloats` (window ≥ 668px). The forced-floating 512–668px range keeps the current overlay; #70 covers narrow screens.
- **What the lock blocks:** only hovers on the menu button. Hovering the sidebar itself, and tapping the menu button, keep working during the animation.

## Changes

### 1. [SidebarProvider.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx): state and timing

- Export `SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS = 500` so the CSS transition in `index.tsx` uses the same value. Add `MENU_HOVER_OPEN_DELAY = 200`.
- Expose `reflows = floatingSidebar && !alwaysFloats`.
- **Menu-button hover goes through the provider.** It currently calls `setHidden(false)` directly in the Titlebar, which also means the sidebar never closes if the mouse doesn't enter it afterwards. Replace that with:
  - a new `hoveringMenuButton` state, added to the existing derived show/hide effect next to `hoveringSidebar` and `hoveringPopover` (lines 60–67). Showing stays immediate, and hiding keeps the 350ms delay.
  - `onMenuButtonHoverStart()`: do nothing if `isAnimatingRef.current` is set. Otherwise start a 200ms timer (kept in a ref). When it fires, check the animation lock again, then `setHoveringMenuButton(true)`.
  - `onMenuButtonHoverEnd()`: clear the timer and `setHoveringMenuButton(false)`. This is never blocked.
  - Clear the timer on unmount.
- **Animation lock:** an effect on `hidden` (skipped on first render via a ref) sets `isAnimatingRef.current = true`, then sets it back to false after `SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS`, clearing any previous timeout. A ref is enough because only event handlers read it.
- Add `reflows`, `onMenuButtonHoverStart` and `onMenuButtonHoverEnd` to the context type, the provider value and `useSidebar()`.

### 2. [sidebar/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx): take up layout space

- If `sidebar.reflows` is true:
  - Use no absolute positioning, so the sidebar is in the flex flow, with `flexShrink: 0`.
  - Use `marginTop: 8` and `marginBottom: 8` in place of `top`/`bottom: 8`, which have no effect without positioning. This keeps the floating card look.
  - Collapse its layout space with `marginRight: hidden ? -width : 0`. Keep `translateX(-100%)` while hidden so the panel is visually hidden before `width` has been measured.
  - Add `margin-right` to the transition list, using `SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS`. The sidebar edge and the content edge then move together.
- Measure `width` by wrapping `<Sidebar />` in an inner `View` with `innerRef` from the existing [useResizeObserver](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useResizeObserver.ts) hook, storing the result in local state. This picks up the user resizing the sidebar, and leaves `Sidebar.tsx` and its `Resizable` untouched.
- Keep the shadow and rounded corners. The issue says not to restyle the panel.
- If `alwaysFloats` is true (narrow) or the sidebar is pinned, the styles stay exactly as they are now.

### 3. [Titlebar.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx#L301-L316): menu button

- `onHoverStart` (mouse): call `sidebar.onMenuButtonHoverStart()` instead of `sidebar.setHidden(false)`.
- Add `onHoverEnd` (mouse) → `sidebar.onMenuButtonHoverEnd()`.
- Leave the `onPress` tap toggle unchanged; it is never blocked.
- Electron/macOS padding for the window buttons (line 295): only apply `paddingLeft: 80` when `floatingSidebar && (sidebar.hidden || !sidebar.reflows)`. When the reflowing sidebar is open, the titlebar no longer sits at the window's left edge.

### 4. Tests

- [SidebarProvider.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.test.ts) uses fake timers, with `useGlobalPref` mocked to `true` for these cases:
  - Hovering the menu button opens the sidebar only after 200ms, not at 199ms.
  - Ending the hover before 200ms means it never opens.
  - Ending the hover after it opened hides the sidebar 350ms later.
  - A hover start within 500ms of `hidden` changing is ignored. A fresh hover start after the 500ms works.
  - Hover end is never blocked.
  - `reflows` is true when the preference is on and the width is 1000. It is false when the width is 600 (`alwaysFloats`) or the preference is off.
- [index.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.test.tsx):
  - Stub `ResizeObserver` with `vi.stubGlobal`, since jsdom doesn't provide it.
  - Add `reflows` and `hidden` to the `setup()` mock.
  - Check that a reflowing wrapper isn't `position: absolute` and has a negative `marginRight` when hidden and 0 when open.
  - Check that the `alwaysFloats` and pinned cases keep their current styles.
- Add a release note in `upcoming-release-notes/` (use the `writing-release-notes` skill).

## Verification

1. `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix`, then `yarn test` (or `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test` for the sidebar tests), all from the repo root.
2. Manual check with `yarn start` → "View demo", with the sidebar unpinned (floating), at about 1200px wide:
   - Rest on the hamburger button: the sidebar opens after about 200ms and the budget shrinks smoothly, with no part of it covered.
   - Sweep the mouse quickly across the button: nothing happens.
   - Move off the sidebar: it closes after 350ms and the budget returns to full width.
   - Hold the cursor where the button slides back to: no reopen/close loop.
   - Resize the sidebar while it's open: the content follows.
   - Check for no horizontal scrollbar during the transition.
   - Pin the sidebar and check it behaves as before.
   - Narrow the window to about 600px: the sidebar overlays as before.
   - Tap toggle (touch emulation in devtools): it still opens and closes, even mid-animation.
3. Confirm the Settings and Bank Sync pages (which use `marginInline: auto` when floating) still centre correctly with the sidebar open.

## Known risk

The budget table re-lays out on every frame of the 0.5s transition. If that's visibly janky on large budgets, record it for #70. Don't change budget components in this issue.
```

```text
  - Collapse its layout space with `marginRight: hidden ? -width : 0`. Keep `translateX(-100%)` while hidden so the panel is visually hidden before `width` has been measured.
  - Add `margin-right` to the transition list, using `SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS`. The sidebar edge and the content edge then move together.
- Measure `width` by wrapping `<Sidebar />` in an inner `View` with `innerRef` from the existing [useResizeObserver](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useResizeObserver.ts) hook, storing the result in local state. This picks up the user resizing the sidebar, and leaves `Sidebar.tsx` and its `Resizable` untouched.
- Keep the shadow and rounded corners. The issue says not to restyle the panel.
- If `alwaysFloats` is true (narrow) or the sidebar is pinned, the styles stay exactly as they are now.

### 3. [Titlebar.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx#L301-L316): menu button

- `onHoverStart` (mouse): call `sidebar.onMenuButtonHoverStart()` instead of `sidebar.setHidden(false)`.
- Add `onHoverEnd` (mouse) → `sidebar.onMenuButtonHoverEnd()`.
- Leave the `onPress` tap toggle unchanged; it is never blocked.
- Electron/macOS padding for the window buttons (line 295): only apply `paddingLeft: 80` when `floatingSidebar && (sidebar.hidden || !sidebar.reflows)`. When the reflowing sidebar is open, the titlebar no longer sits at the window's left edge.

### 4. Tests

- [SidebarProvider.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.test.ts) uses fake timers, with `useGlobalPref` mocked to `true` for these cases:
  - Hovering the menu button opens the sidebar only after 200ms, not at 199ms.
  - Ending the hover before 200ms means it never opens.
  - Ending the hover after it opened hides the sidebar 350ms later.
  - A hover start within 500ms of `hidden` changing is ignored. A fresh hover start after the 500ms works.
  - Hover end is never blocked.
  - `reflows` is true when the preference is on and the width is 1000. It is false when the width is 600 (`alwaysFloats`) or the preference is off.
- [index.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.test.tsx):
  - Stub `ResizeObserver` with `vi.stubGlobal`, since jsdom doesn't provide it.
  - Add `reflows` and `hidden` to the `setup()` mock.
  - Check that a reflowing wrapper isn't `position: absolute` and has a negative `marginRight` when hidden and 0 when open.
  - Check that the `alwaysFloats` and pinned cases keep their current styles.
- Add a release note in `upcoming-release-notes/` (use the `writing-release-notes` skill).

## Verification

1. `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix`, then `yarn test` (or `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test` for the sidebar tests), all from the repo root.
2. Manual check with `yarn start` → "View demo", with the sidebar unpinned (floating), at about 1200px wide:
   - Rest on the hamburger button: the sidebar opens after about 200ms and the budget shrinks smoothly, with no part of it covered.
   - Sweep the mouse quickly across the button: nothing happens.
   - Move off the sidebar: it closes after 350ms and the budget returns to full width.
   - Hold the cursor where the button slides back to: no reopen/close loop.
   - Resize the sidebar while it's open: the content follows.
   - Check for no horizontal scrollbar during the transition.
   - Pin the sidebar and check it behaves as before.
   - Narrow the window to about 600px: the sidebar overlays as before.
   - Tap toggle (touch emulation in devtools): it still opens and closes, even mid-animation.
3. Confirm the Settings and Bank Sync pages (which use `marginInline: auto` when floating) still centre correctly with the sidebar open.

## Known risk

The budget table re-lays out on every frame of the 0.5s transition. If that's visibly janky on large budgets, record it for #70. Don't change budget components in this issue.
```

```typescript
// @ts-strict-ignore
import React, {
  createContext,
  useContext,
  useEffect,
  useLayoutEffect,
  useMemo,
  useRef,
  useState,
} from 'react';
import type { Dispatch, ReactNode, SetStateAction } from 'react';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';

import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

const HOVER_HIDE_DELAY = 350;
const MENU_HOVER_OPEN_DELAY = 200;
export const SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS = 500;

type SidebarContextValue = {
  hidden: boolean;
  setHidden: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
  setHoveringSidebar: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
  onMenuButtonHoverStart: () => void;
  onMenuButtonHoverEnd: () => void;
  floating: boolean;
  alwaysFloats: boolean;
  reflows: boolean;
};

const SidebarContext = createContext<SidebarContextValue>(null);

type SidebarProviderProps = {
  children: ReactNode;
};

export function SidebarProvider({ children }: SidebarProviderProps) {
  const [floatingSidebar] = useGlobalPref('floatingSidebar');
  const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(true);
  const { width } = useResponsive();
  const alwaysFloats = width < 668;
  const floating = floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats;
  // When floating by choice (not forced by a narrow window), the open sidebar
  // takes up layout space so the main content shrinks instead of being covered.
  const reflows = !!floatingSidebar && !alwaysFloats;
  const dispatch = useDispatch();

  // A dropdown menu opened from the sidebar (e.g. BudgetName's) renders in a
  // portal, outside the sidebar's own DOM subtree, so hovering it never
  // triggers the sidebar's onMouseOver/onMouseLeave. Track hover of the
  // sidebar and of any open popover separately, then derive `hidden` from
  // both combined, so the sidebar (and its menu) stay visible while either
  // is being used, and only hide together once neither is hovered anymore.
  const [hoveringSidebar, setHoveringSidebar] = useState(false);
  const [hoveringPopover, setHoveringPopover] = useState(false);
  const [hoveringMenuButton, setHoveringMenuButton] = useState(false);

  // While the sidebar animates open or closed, the titlebar's menu button
  // slides with the main content and can end up under a resting cursor.
  // Ignore menu button hovers until the animation finishes so that can't
  // start an open/close loop.
  const isAnimatingRef = useRef(false);
  const isFirstRenderRef = useRef(true);
  const menuHoverTimeoutRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (isFirstRenderRef.current) {
      isFirstRenderRef.current = false;
      return;
    }
    isAnimatingRef.current = true;
    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
      isAnimatingRef.current = false;
    }, SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS);
    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
  }, [hidden]);

  useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(menuHoverTimeoutRef.current), []);

  function onMenuButtonHoverStart() {
    if (isAnimatingRef.current) {
      return;
    }
    clearTimeout(menuHoverTimeoutRef.current);
    // Only open once the cursor rests on the button, so a mouse passing over
    // it on the way somewhere else doesn't open the sidebar.
    menuHoverTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
      if (!isAnimatingRef.current) {
        setHoveringMenuButton(true);
      }
    }, MENU_HOVER_OPEN_DELAY);
  }

  function onMenuButtonHoverEnd() {
    clearTimeout(menuHoverTimeoutRef.current);
    setHoveringMenuButton(false);
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    function handlePointerOver(e: PointerEvent) {
      const target = e.target as Element | null;
      setHoveringPopover(!!target?.closest?.('[data-popover]'));
    }
    document.addEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
  }, []);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (hoveringSidebar || hoveringPopover || hoveringMenuButton) {
      setHidden(false);
      return;
    }
    const timeout = setTimeout(() => setHidden(true), HOVER_HIDE_DELAY);
    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
  }, [hoveringSidebar, hoveringPopover, hoveringMenuButton]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (hidden && !hoveringPopover) {
      dispatch(closeContextMenu());
    }
  }, [hidden, hoveringPopover, dispatch]);

  return (
    <SidebarContext.Provider
      value={{
        hidden,
        setHidden,
        setHoveringSidebar,
        onMenuButtonHoverStart,
        onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
        floating,
        alwaysFloats,
        reflows,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </SidebarContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useSidebar() {
  const {
    hidden,
    setHidden,
    setHoveringSidebar,
    onMenuButtonHoverStart,
    onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
    floating,
    alwaysFloats,
    reflows,
  } = useContext(SidebarContext);

  return useMemo(
    () => ({
      hidden,
      setHidden,
      setHoveringSidebar,
      onMenuButtonHoverStart,
      onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
      floating,
      alwaysFloats,
      reflows,
    }),
    [
      hidden,
      setHidden,
      setHoveringSidebar,
      onMenuButtonHoverStart,
      onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
      floating,
      alwaysFloats,
      reflows,
    ],
  );
}
```

```typescript
import React, { useState } from 'react';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';
import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';

import { useResizeObserver } from '#hooks/useResizeObserver';

import { Sidebar } from './Sidebar';
import { SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS, useSidebar } from './SidebarProvider';

export function FloatableSidebar() {
  const sidebar = useSidebar();
  const { isNarrowWidth } = useResponsive();
  const [sidebarWidth, setSidebarWidth] = useState(0);
  const sidebarRef = useResizeObserver<HTMLDivElement>(rect => {
    setSidebarWidth(rect.width);
  });

  const sidebarShouldFloat = sidebar.floating;
  // A reflowing sidebar stays in the flex layout next to the main content and
  // collapses its own width while hidden, so the content resizes alongside it.
  const sidebarReflows = sidebar.reflows;
  const transition = `${SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS}ms`;

  return isNarrowWidth ? null : (
    <View
      onMouseOver={
        sidebarShouldFloat
          ? e => {
              e.stopPropagation();
              sidebar.setHoveringSidebar(true);
            }
          : undefined
      }
      onMouseLeave={
        sidebarShouldFloat ? () => sidebar.setHoveringSidebar(false) : undefined
      }
      style={{
        position: sidebarShouldFloat && !sidebarReflows ? 'absolute' : undefined,
        top: 8,
        // If not floating, the -50 takes into account the transform below
        bottom: sidebarShouldFloat ? 8 : -50,
        ...(sidebarReflows && {
          flexShrink: 0,
          marginTop: 8,
          marginBottom: 8,
          marginRight: sidebar.hidden ? -sidebarWidth : 0,
        }),
        zIndex: 1001,
        borderRadius: sidebarShouldFloat ? '0 6px 6px 0' : 0,
        overflow: 'hidden',
        boxShadow:
          !sidebarShouldFloat || sidebar.hidden
            ? 'none'
            : '0 15px 30px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.25), 0 3px 15px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.5)',
        transform: `translateY(${!sidebarShouldFloat ? -8 : 0}px)
                      translateX(${
                        sidebarShouldFloat && sidebar.hidden ? '-100' : '0'
                      }%)`,
        transition: `transform ${transition}, box-shadow ${transition}, border-radius ${transition}, bottom ${transition}, margin-right ${transition}`,
      }}
    >
      <View innerRef={sidebarRef} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
        <Sidebar />
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

I've implemented #69 using approach (a). When the unpinned sidebar opens, the budget now shrinks to sit beside it; when it closes, the budget grows back to full width. I haven't tried it in the running app yet — tests, typecheck and lint pass, but the browser checklist below still needs doing.

**How it behaves now:**
- **200ms hover delay:** the sidebar opens only if the mouse rests on the menu button for 200ms. A quick pass over it does nothing.
- **Animation lock:** hovering the menu button is ignored while the 0.5s open/close animation runs, so the button sliding back under a still cursor can't start an open/close loop. As agreed, hovering the sidebar itself and tapping the menu button still work during the animation.
- **Narrow windows:** below 668px wide, where the sidebar is forced to float, it still covers the content as before. That's left for #70.
- **One fix to existing behaviour:** before, opening the sidebar from the menu button left it open until the mouse went into the sidebar and back out. Now it also closes 350ms after the mouse leaves the button. This applies in every floating mode.
- **macOS desktop app:** the titlebar no longer leaves space for the window buttons while the reflowing sidebar is open, since it's no longer at the window's left edge. I haven't tested this.

**Files changed:**
- [SidebarProvider.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx): the hover delay, the animation lock, and the menu-button hover now feeding the existing show/hide timing.
- [sidebar/index.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/index.tsx): while floating at normal widths, the sidebar takes up real space in the layout and gives that space back as it closes, in step with its slide-out. It measures its own width, so resizing the sidebar while it's open works and `Sidebar.tsx` is unchanged.
- [Titlebar.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx): the menu button reports hover start and end to the provider; the tap toggle is unchanged.
- Release note: [resize-content-with-floating-sidebar.md](upcoming-release-notes/resize-content-with-floating-sidebar.md).

**Tests:** 12 new sidebar tests cover the 200ms delay, the hide timing, the lock, which modes reflow, and the sidebar's layout styles. All 23 sidebar tests and the full web suite (928) pass.
